Did not flag ordering specifically; flagged absence of tests for the new path

issues.description: OutputImageRawFrame uses raw bytes from a PIL image whose mode may not be RGB while declaring format='RGB'
issues.detail: Image.open(io.BytesIO(part.inline_data.data)) may return an image in mode RGBA, P, L, or CMYK depending on what Gemini emits (PNG with alpha is common). image.tobytes() returns the raw buffer in the image's native mode, not RGB, so the OutputImageRawFrame's declared format='RGB' lies about the byte layout. Downstream consumers expecting width*height*3 bytes will get garbled colors, size mismatches, or silent corruption. Fix by calling image.convert('RGB') before tobytes(), or by passing the actual mode through.

issues.description: Module-import-time monkey-patch of genai._api_client.READ_BUFFER_SIZE mutates third-party private state unconditionally
issues.detail: The line `genai._api_client.READ_BUFFER_SIZE = 5 * 1024 * 1024` reaches into a leading-underscore submodule of google-genai at import time and is self-labeled 'Temporary hack'. It poisons global SDK state for every consumer of google-genai in the process — not just users of image models — has no hasattr guard, no version sentinel, no scoping, and no tracking issue. Any future google-genai release that renames or relocates the attribute raises AttributeError at import and breaks every Google service in pipecat. At minimum add a hasattr guard, justify the 5 MiB bound, and link an upstream issue; preferably move to scoped client configuration or a public API.

issues.description: Default model silently changed from gemini-2.0-flash to gemini-2.5-flash, altering behavior for every existing caller
issues.detail: The constructor default changes the model for any caller who did not pass an explicit model=. Cost, latency, token accounting, tool-call shape, and the new thinking-budget gating all shift. The CHANGELOG records it only under 'Changed' as a one-liner; there is no deprecation path, runtime warning, or major-version bump. This is also bundled into a feature PR titled 'image generation' rather than being split out. Either keep the old default and document the new recommended value, emit a one-time logger.warning when the default is taken, or split into its own PR with a louder breaking-default note.

issues.description: Image-model detection uses fragile substring match `'image' in self._model_name` rather than a named capability predicate
issues.detail: The check inside _maybe_unset_thinking_budget conflates 'model name happens to contain the substring image' with 'this is an image-generating model that does not support a thinking budget'. It will both falsely match unrelated future models (e.g. gemini-2.6-pro-imagen-eval) and miss future image models named differently. Lift the capability into an explicit allowlist, a small dispatch table, or a method like _model_supports_image_output(name)/ModelCapabilities.GENERATES_IMAGES so the predicate is named, testable, and reusable in both the thinking-budget branch and the inline_data branch.

issues.description: New image-emission branch has no specified contract for ordering, multi-image responses, error handling, or context/history semantics
issues.detail: The new elif pushes OutputImageRawFrame inline within the candidate-parts loop with no stated ordering relative to LLMTextFrame emissions, no behavior for multiple inline_data parts, no try/except around Image.open (so PIL.UnidentifiedImageError on malformed payloads aborts the entire turn), no size cap if the 5 MiB hack proves insufficient, no mime_type check (trusting any inline_data to be an image rather than e.g. audio), and no decision about whether the image flows into the assistant context aggregator for replay/history. Downstream consumers have to reverse-engineer the producer's behavior. Add a docstring naming the postconditions, wrap decoding in try/except, validate mime_type, and decide explicitly whether images are part of conversational history or a side channel.

issues.description: _process_context part-dispatch cascade is the wrong data structure for a growing set of part types
issues.detail: _process_context walks candidates -> content.parts -> branches on text / function_call / inline_data inside an already long method. Each part type is a small stateless transform from a Gemini Part into an outbound Frame; a small dispatch table or per-part-type handler functions would make each new modality (image, audio, video) a one-line addition rather than another elif on a growing pyramid. The data shape dominates and the algorithm should follow.

issues.description: No unit-test coverage for the new image-decoding branch or the thinking-budget gating
issues.detail: A new control-flow branch in _process_context opens bytes with PIL, constructs a frame, and pushes it downstream; a new branch in _maybe_unset_thinking_budget toggles thinking config. The diff contains zero unit tests for either. The example script is not a test — it requires a live API key and a transport. A unit test feeding a synthetic Part with inline_data.data set to a known PNG/JPEG (including an RGBA PNG to surface the format='RGB' bug) and asserting the resulting OutputImageRawFrame's size, format, and byte length would catch the P0 above. Without tests the postcondition is asserted, not demonstrated.

issues.description: Three logically independent changes squashed into one PR (image feature, default-model bump, dependency widening)
issues.detail: The diff does (1) add image-output handling to GoogleLLMService, (2) bump the default model from gemini-2.0-flash to gemini-2.5-flash, and (3) widen google-* dependency specifiers from `~=` to `>=,<major`. Each has different blast radius, different reverts, and different reviewer audiences. Split into three patches with three commit messages and three revert points; this also lets each change carry its own changelog rationale and test matrix.

issues.description: Dependency specifiers widened from `~=1.24.0` to `>=1.41.0,<2` (and similarly for speech/tts) without recorded test matrix or rationale
issues.detail: Moving from a compatible-release constraint to a half-open <2 range trades reproducibility for flexibility across the whole google extra. Combined with the genai._api_client.READ_BUFFER_SIZE monkey-patch, any minor release of google-genai inside [1.41, 2) can silently remove or rename the patched attribute. The diff records no rationale and no test coverage for the new allowed range. Pin tighter (closer to what was actually tested) until the buffer-size hack is removed upstream, and document the API surface depended on.

issues.description: PIL Image and io imports for the new branch are not visible in the diff hunk
issues.detail: The new code calls Image.open(io.BytesIO(...)) but the diff does not show those imports being added. If they are already present in the module via another path this is fine, but it cannot be confirmed from the diff alone, and the new code path also depends on PIL being in the `google` extra's dependency closure. If missing, a NameError will occur only when an image part is received — a latent failure mode that text-only tests will never trigger.

issues.description: Stray blank line added in __init__ with no semantic content
issues.detail: The diff inserts an empty line between `self._http_options = http_options` and `self._create_client(...)`. Pure noise that will live in blame forever. Remove it.

issues.description: Example file docstring conflates Gemini API with Google Cloud Speech/TTS and under-documents required env vars
issues.detail: The header says 'Gemini for both LLM, STT and TTS' but the example uses GoogleSTTService/GoogleTTSService (Google Cloud, not Gemini). The example also requires GOOGLE_TEST_CREDENTIALS in addition to GOOGLE_API_KEY but only documents the latter in the 'Make sure to set' block. The headline feature of the file is image generation but the docstring does not lead with that. Since this file is the canonical onboarding artifact for the feature, the inaccuracy matters.

issues.description: Example file copyright header dates are inconsistent with project convention (2024-2025 on a 2026 file)
issues.detail: The new example uses `Copyright (c) 2024-2025` while the PR lands in 2026. Not a correctness issue, but a small signal about long-lived artifact maintenance and the example will be the user-facing entry point for the feature.

synthesis.summary: All six reviewers independently converged on two P0 defects: (1) the new image branch passes `image.tobytes()` with a hard-coded `format='RGB'` while the PIL image's actual mode may be RGBA/P/L/CMYK, silently producing wrong pixel bytes whenever Gemini returns a non-RGB image; and (2) module-import-time mutation of the private third-party attribute `genai._api_client.READ_BUFFER_SIZE`, self-labeled 'Temporary hack', which globally poisons google-genai for every consumer in the process and will break at import the day the attribute is renamed. All six also flagged the silent default-model bump from gemini-2.0-flash to gemini-2.5-flash and the fragile `'image' in self._model_name` substring capability check. The strongest preserved disagreement is on the severity of the monkey-patch (Hickey/Torvalds/Dijkstra call it P0 and refuse-on-sight; Knuth/Liskov/Pike call it P1, fixable with hasattr guards and scoping) and on whether the default-model change is P1 'silent breaking contract change' (Knuth/Hickey/Liskov/Dijkstra) versus P2 'behavior change disguised as a feature add' (Pike). Secondary unanimous-ish concerns: no unit tests for the new branch, no error handling for malformed image payloads, undocumented ordering between image and text frames within a turn, three independent changes squashed into one PR, and a dependency-range widening from `~=` to `>=,<major` that compounds the monkey-patch risk.
